A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same OneForecast study. All 40 pages, including Appendices A–G, provide readable and corresponding text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original global forecasting results in Table 1, regional evaluations in Figure 6, ablations in Table 3, and additional empirical results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v4 retains these original forecasting experiments, ablations, ensemble evaluations, and supplementary empirical results.

M1.justification: The region-refined graph, multi-stream messaging, neural nested grid, training losses, and inference procedures are unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same WeatherBench2/ERA5 data, variables, regional coverage, typhoon cases, and forecasting tasks. The corrected source-grid dimensions do not establish different data or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and FuXi in Table 1, Graph-EFM in Figure 6, and the Appendix G comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 revises the reported full-global dimensions of the 0.25° ERA5 source data from 721 × 240 to 721 × 1440. This corrects a stated data setting; the PDFs do not establish rerunning experiments. The 120 × 240 regional crop in Appendix E.1, splits, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Section 3.6, spectral analyses, efficiency analysis, typhoon cases, and long-term forecasting analyses retain the same questions and evidence.

E5.justification: The descriptions of 50-member perturbed-initial-condition ensembles and averaging are unchanged. Neither version adds training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Result tables and plotted findings, including Appendix G, are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains OneForecast normalized RMSE values of 0.0549 at six hours and 0.5918 at ten days.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1, the theorem and proof in Appendix A, method equations, and metric definitions in Appendix F.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified global-regional forecasting, adaptive information propagation, extreme-event prediction, and long-term forecasting.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations are unchanged, including the discussion of boundary information, over-smoothing, and the limitation imposed by low-resolution inputs on cyclone prediction.

D1.justification: The 721 × 1440 correction in Section 3.1 improves the technical description of the ERA5 source grid. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing instructions, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, Appendix B literature discussion, and positioning relative to Graph-EFM and other forecasting approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the grid-dimension correction in Section 3.1 and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. Paragraph wording, terminology, and section and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 30 figures and seven tables retain their displays, captions, numbering, and placement. The page layout is preserved; small rendering differences do not constitute a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects the full-global ERA5 grid to 721 × 1440, consistent with the stated 0.25° resolution. This removes a concrete inconsistency and modestly improves technical accuracy and clarity about the source data. The methods, supporting evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
